title: Crispi Butternut Half-Moons with Orange-Pepita Glaze
description: Tender butternut half-moons are coated in a smooth orange and pumpkin-seed glaze with a little ground sumac.
equipment: Ninja Crispi PowerPod with US Bake preset and 6-cup glass container

ingredients.name: butternut squash neck
ingredients.note: Peel, halve lengthwise and slice into 1/4-inch half-moons.

ingredients.name: low-sodium mushroom broth
ingredients.note: Choose plain broth made with mushrooms and water.

ingredients.name: smooth unsalted pumpkin seed paste
ingredients.note: Use finely milled pepita butter without coarse pieces.

steps.title: Set up the Crispi
steps.text: Use the room-temperature 6-cup Ninja glass container without its crisper plate or an adapter. Leave off the storage lid. Load the container before starting the PowerPod.

steps.title: Moisten the squash
steps.text: Toss {squash} with {broth} in the unheated glass. Nestle the half-moons into the liquid in a shallow layer.

steps.title: Braise on Bake
steps.text: Seat the PowerPod and select Bake. After 8 minutes, turn the top pieces into the broth. Cook another 6–12 minutes until the thickest half-moon is tender enough to split with a spoon.

steps.title: Make the orange base
steps.text: Transfer the squash to a covered serving bowl. Ladle the warm cooking liquid into the HexClad and whisk in {orange}, {sumac} and {honey}.

steps.title: Smooth the seed paste
steps.text: Whisk {seed_paste} with a spoonful of warm sauce base in a small bowl until smooth, then return it to the pan.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the base to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Glaze the half-moons
steps.text: Turn the warm half-moons gently in the glaze and divide between two bowls, spooning the rest of the glaze over them.

notes: Make ahead: Slice the squash up to two days ahead and keep it covered in the refrigerator. Refrigerate the finished dish for up to 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze in the glaze for up to 6 weeks. The half-moons soften after thawing and can be served as a spoonable mash. Fridge reheat: Warm a single portion, covered, in the HexClad with a splash of broth or water. Stir or turn gently and heat to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Use the same covered reheating method and heat the center to 165°F. Option A uses orange and sumac. For gentler Option B, replace the juice with smooth pear puree and leave out the sumac; the honey and seed paste carry the glaze. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 119 kcal, 3.4 g protein, 22.9 g total carbohydrate, 2.8 g fat, 3.3 g fiber, 13 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.

steps.title: Allow for oven timing
steps.text: Use the first time given as a check. A covered metal dish may need 3–10 minutes longer; check tenderness or the center temperature every 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Heat the covered baking dish
steps.text: Preheat Samsung Bake to 350°F. Use a small metal baking dish and a fitted cover or foil to retain moisture.

steps.title: Moisten the squash
steps.text: Toss {squash} with {broth} in the metal baking dish. Nestle the half-moons into the liquid in a shallow layer.

steps.title: Braise on Bake
